**Group:** Listing intelligence

### `pickup-location`
- **Purpose:** resolve where an item really is from every signal in the listing, and publish only the town or area.
- **Does / does not:** the owner's "Where an item really is" (`nabvy/docs/decisions.md:144-153`). Rules first, over the location field (the card's city page and town label), the coarse detail coordinates, and place names and postcodes in the title and description, for example "collection from Bognor" (`nabvy/docs/decisions.md:145`) or an autofilled postcode typed earlier that day (`nabvy/docs/decisions.md:146`). Records a conflict when they disagree. AI runs at most once per listing version, shared by every user, only where the rules cannot decide, on the `quote-redaction` copy of the text, and its output is validated against a Zod schema before use (`nabvy/docs/decisions.md:153`). The resolved point, its basis (`field | text | ai | fallback`), confidence and any full postcode or street stay in its tables; only the town or area, marked approximate when uncertain, reaches a `v_` view or user-facing output (`nabvy/docs/decisions.md:153`). Distance filters, the map and the worth-the-trip hints use the resolved location through the exported `pointsFor(listingIds)`, never through a view (`actor-integration.md` 3.3). It computes no distance (`location`) and labels nothing (`suspected-labels` reads its conflict flag). This card is a placeholder until the listing-location draft lands (`nabvy/docs/handoff.md:94`).
- **Inputs:** `detail-evidence.changed`, `listing-ingest.first-seen`; `v_listings`, `v_current`, `v_text`; `v_city_pages`; `pointForPostcode()`; `v_throttle`; `redact()`; `is_suppressed()`.
- **Outputs:** `pickup-location.resolved` (listing IDs); `pointsFor(listingIds)` for `spec-match`, `notifier` and procedures; `erase(listingIds)`.
- **Owns:** `resolutions` (listing, evidence_hash, lat, lng, basis, confidence, conflict, town_or_area, approximate, rule_version), `calls` (listing, evidence_hash, model, prompt_version, cost).
- **Views:** internal `v_areas` (listing_id, town_or_area, approximate, conflict, basis); user-facing `app.v_pickup_location_areas` (listing_id, town_or_area, approximate).
- **Contracts:** `PickupLocationBasis`, `PickupLocationOutput` (model output), `PickupLocationResolvedEvent`.
- **Depends on:** `switches`, `listing-ingest`, `detail-evidence`, `city-pages`, `location`, `quote-redaction`, `spend-governor`, `cost-meter`, `listing-suppression`.
- **When off (its AI step stays off with `parts-ai`, question 12):** readers use the coarse detail coordinates, then the city page, and say "approximate"; there is no location-conflict signal for "too good to be true".
- **Tests and fixtures:** a Chichester location field with "collection from Bognor" in the text resolves to Bognor with a conflict; a postcode in the text never appears in any view; the town label fallback; replay writes nothing.
- **Priority and phase:** MVP (`nabvy/docs/decisions.md:140,144-153`).
- **Sources:** `nabvy/docs/decisions.md:20,142-153`; `actor-integration.md` section 8, change 9.
- **Open questions:** 12; `actor-integration.md` question 20.
